# Prerequisites

- Package Installation
- Data Availability
- Correct Fiducial Alignment
- Aligned Tissue positions (`rds` or `csv` file, or `data.frame` object,
incl. information regarding orientation adjustments)

For ensuring the prerequisites are met, we recommend, checking out the 
[Fiducial Detection](%\VignetteIndexEntry{visiumSpatialSolutions: Fiducial_Detection}) vignette, first.

---

## Vignette Datasets

- [Visium_FFPE_Human_Ovarian_Cancer](https://www.10xgenomics.com/datasets/human-ovarian-cancer-1-standard)
- [CytAssist_11mm_FFPE_Human_Ovarian_Carcinoma](https://www.10xgenomics.com/datasets/human-ovarian-cancer-11-mm-capture-area-ffpe-2-standard)

The required files can be downloaded and extracted using the function `download_vignette_files()` as demonstrated in the 
[Fiducial Detection](%\VignetteIndexEntry{visiumSpatialSolutions: Fiducial_Detection}) vignette. 

Alternatively, you can use your own data.

---

## Settings

```{r settings}
# load packages
library(dplyr)
library(visiumSpatialSolutions)

# define directories
output_dir <- file.path(getwd(), "data")
figures_dir <- file.path(getwd(), "figures")
```

---

# Visium spatial-array geometry

The derivation and visualization of candidate physical coordinate
reconstructions for 6.5 mm and 11 mm Visium array are available in the
[Reconstruction_Models](https://Zockimonster.github.io/visiumSpatialSolutions/).

The JSON-assisted coordinate dimensions are derived in [Spatial_Alignment](https://Zockimonster.github.io/visiumSpatialSolutions/).

---

## Define Array-specific settings

**Small array**

```{r settings-for-loading-small-array-input}
L <- 6500
visium_sample <- "Visium_FFPE_Human_Ovarian_Cancer"
figures_sample <- file.path(figures_dir, visium_sample)
mtx_type <- "h5"
mtx_name <- "filtered"
img_res <- "hires"
```
**Large array**

```{r settings-for-loading-large-array-input}
L <- 11000
visium_sample <- "CytAssist_11mm_FFPE_Human_Ovarian_Carcinoma"
figures_sample <- file.path(figures_dir, visium_sample)
mtx_type <- "h5"
mtx_name <- "filtered"
img_res <- "hires"
```

--- 

## Load input data

```{r load-input, eval=FALSE}
spex <- load_spex(visium_dir=output_dir, visium_sample=visium_sample, matrix_name=mtx_name, matrix_file_format=mtx_type, image_resolution=img_res)
tp_aligned <- load_aligned_tp(file_dir=output_dir, visium_sample=visium_sample)
```

---

### Spatial Conversion

To align the spot positions with the spatially resolved image, we define the settings & use the function `spatial_conversion`:

```{r spatial-conversion, eval=FALSE}
sfe <- spatial_conversion(aligned_tp=tp_aligned, spex=spex, L_capture_area=L, image_resolution =img_res)
```

**Spatial containment:
The issue regarding the spots not being fully contained by the capture 
area using the default `spatial_geometry` with `hex100` is expected, so far.**

To create the spatially resolved plot using the colGeometry for `spatial_pixels`,
we can use the function `create_sfe_plot`:

```{r create-sfe-plot, eval=FALSE}
sfe_plot <- create_sfe_plot(sfe=sfe, image_resolution= img_res)
```

Optionally, the spatially resolved plot can be saved to the `figures_sample` directory, using:

```{r save-sfe-plot, eval=FALSE}
ggplot2::ggsave(filename = file.path(figures_sample, "spatially_resolved_plot.png"), 
                plot= sfe_plot, width = 6, height = 6, units = "in")
```


```{r plot-sfe, echo=FALSE, out.height="40%", fig.align="center", fig.cap="**Spatially resolved Image with aligned Spot Positions.**"}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(figures_sample,  "spatially_resolved_plot.png"))
```

---

### Interactive Spot Selection


The `SpatialFeatureExperiment` object with the spatially aligned array and pixel positions can further be used for interactive spot selection,
with the tissue image overlaid by the spatially aligned `colGeometry` as specified in the argument `geom_id`.
The selected barcodes can easily be downloaded as `csv` file using the `Download selected spots` button within the application. 
The `download_filename` can be adjusted in the function call, but also it can be changed when the download option is chosen. 

```{r interactive-spot-selection, eval=FALSE}
p_ia <- prepare_interactive_spot_selection(sfe, image_resolution =img_res, download_filename = "selected_A.csv")
shiny::shinyApp(p_ia$user_interface, p_ia$server_settings)
```

To reload selected barcodes and

- add this information to the spatially aligned tissue positions, we can use: 

```{r add-selected-barcodes, eval=FALSE}
# out_dir equals the directory, you selected for downloading the selected tissue positions
# since we selected the output_dir, we use
out_dir <- output_dir
selected_A <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "selected_A.csv"))
tp_aligned$selected_A <- ifelse(tp_aligned$barcode %in% selected_A$barcode, 1, 0) 
table(tp_aligned$selected_A, useNA="ifany")
```


- add these to the `SpatialFeatureExperiment` object, we can use:

```{r add-to-sfe, eval=FALSE}
SpatialFeatureExperiment::colGeometry(sfe, "spatial_pixels")$selected_A <- tp_aligned$selected_A[match(colnames(sfe, "spatial_pixels"), tp_aligned$barcode)]
```


### Multiple Sets of selected Spots

This application can easily be used for selecting distinct sets of spots, download the barcodes for each selection, and combine this information, afterwards:

Selection of B spots:

```{r selection-B, eval=FALSE}
p_ia <- prepare_interactive_spot_selection(sfe, image_resolution = img_res, download_filename="selected_B.csv")
shiny::shinyApp(p_ia$user_interface, p_ia$server_settings)
```

Afterwards, we can add and combine this information in the aligned tissue position data, using:

```{r add-B, eval=FALSE}
selected_B <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "selected_B.csv"))
tp_aligned$selected_B <- ifelse(tp_aligned$barcode %in% selected_B$barcode, 1, 0)
SpatialFeatureExperiment::colGeometry(sfe, "spatial_pixels")$selected_B <- tp_aligned$selected_B[match(colnames(sfe, "spatial_pixels"), tp_aligned$barcode)]
table(tp_aligned$selected_A, tp_aligned$selected_B, useNA="ifany")
```

Which can be further combined into one column, using

```{r one_column-AB, eval=FALSE}
tp_aligned$selected_AB <- rep(NA_character_, nrow(tp_aligned))
tp_aligned$selected_AB[tp_aligned$selected_A == 0 & tp_aligned$selected_B== 0] <- "none"
tp_aligned$selected_AB[tp_aligned$selected_A == 1 & tp_aligned$selected_B== 0] <- "A"
tp_aligned$selected_AB[tp_aligned$selected_A == 0 & tp_aligned$selected_B== 1] <- "B"
tp_aligned$selected_AB[tp_aligned$selected_A == 1 & tp_aligned$selected_B== 1] <- "both"
table(tp_aligned$selected_AB, useNA="ifany")
```

To create a spatially resolved plot for the combined spot selection, we can add this information to the `colGeometry` of the sfe object, and use:

```{r add-AB-to-sfe, eval=FALSE}
SpatialFeatureExperiment::colGeometry(sfe, "spatial_pixels")$selected_AB <- tp_aligned$selected_AB[match(colnames(sfe, "spatial_pixels"), tp_aligned$barcode)]
AB_plot <- create_sfe_plot(sfe, image_resolution =img_res, color_by="selected_AB", plot_title="AB Spot Selection", color_source = "geometry")
```

Optionally, the plot with the spatially resolved spot selection can be saved to the `figures_sample` directory, using:

```{r save-sfe-selection-plot, eval= FALSE}
ggplot2::ggsave(filename = file.path(figures_sample, "spatially_resolved_spot_selection.png"), 
                plot= AB_plot, width = 6, height = 6, units = "in")
```

Exemplary, we created one plot for 2 spot selections for the small sample:

```{r plot-sfe-selection-small, echo=FALSE, out.height="40%", fig.align="center", fig.cap="**Spatially resolved Image with aligned Spot Selection.**"}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(figures_dir, "Visium_FFPE_Human_Ovarian_Cancer",  "spatially_resolved_spot_selection.png"))
```
